name: Mox Diamond
oracle_text:
If this artifact would enter, you may discard a land card instead. If you do, put this artifact onto the battlefield. If you don't, put it into its owner's graveyard.
{T}: Add one mana of any color.
blocked_sentences: If this artifact would enter, you may discard a land card instead. If you do, put this artifact onto the battlefield. If you don't, put it into its owner's graveyard.

needs.what: a replacement of the permanent's own arrival that can redirect the DESTINATION of the zone change on the answer to an optional price. Paid -- here `{"discard_selector": {"types": ["Land"]}}`, the cost vocabulary the DSL already has -- the artifact finishes entering the battlefield; declined, it goes to its owner's graveyard instead and never enters at all, so no `self_enters`/`permanent_enters` trigger anywhere sees it, no state-based action can bin it, and it is never on the battlefield to be sacrificed or bounced in response. Concretely: a `destination` (or `else_zone`) field on the enters replacement beside the existing `unless_cost`, plus a `move_object` path that can end somewhere other than the battlefield, plus the price being a *condition of arrival* rather than a way to avoid a modification. It must apply on EVERY arrival, from any zone -- cast, reanimated, blinked -- not only when the card is cast or played.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `ReplacementModel.event` (src/automtg/cards/schema.py:664) is a closed Literal of five: `self_enters`, `self_enters_tapped`, `self_enters_with_counters`, `self_enters_prepared`, `self_enters_as_copy`. Its own docstring says every one of them modifies the permanent that is *already arriving*, and `zones._enter_battlefield` bears that out -- it runs them after the object is on the battlefield and reads nothing from `modify` but `tapped`, `counters`, `prepared` and `copying`. There is no `graveyard` destination anywhere in that code path. The nearest miss is `unless_cost` (schema.py:730, offered by `zones.offer_enters_costs`), which is genuinely a price asked as the permanent enters and would carry Mox Diamond's discard verbatim -- but paying it only *suppresses a modification* ("enters tapped unless you pay 3 life"); declining leaves the permanent arriving either way, so it cannot express "if you don't, it never enters". It is also asked from exactly two call sites, `game._play_land` and `stack._place_after_resolution`, so even if it could redirect, a Mox Diamond returned from the graveyard or blinked would skip the question entirely -- while the printed card replaces every arrival. The card-level cost keys are the wrong layer twice over: `additional_optional` / `additional_cost` are CAST costs, so they miss those same non-cast arrivals, and neither branch matches the printed card -- a mandatory discard would make the artifact uncastable with no land in hand (it is castable; it just dies on the way), and an optional one left unpaid would still let it enter. `replace_leaves_battlefield` and `replace_deaths` are the only existing destination-rewriting replacements and both fire on the way *out*, so they cannot see a permanent that must never arrive; `replace_token_creation` rewrites what is created but, as its docstring notes, deliberately handles the no-object-yet case for tokens only. Carrying the line as a `self_enters` triggered ability running `may` + `discard` + `sacrifice` is exactly the approximation the rules forbid: the artifact would really enter, every other enters trigger would see it, and it would reach the graveyard *from* the battlefield rather than never having been there.
